Instead respondent has made an allegation against the petitioner that she has not taken any interest in the education of the daughter without understanding that the petitioner had an infant to look after, a job to attend, a house to run and she was over burdened and could not attend to all her responsibilities effectively. Further respondent has contended that, petitioner did not file any complaint against him till she filed this petition and there was no impediment for the petitioner to lodge a complaint against him in USA where the police and Courts are more accessible. Since, petitioner did not file any complaint against him itself proves that she has filed a false case against him. Further just because a delay has been made by the petitioner in filing the complaint cannot prove that the complaint filed by her is false. The respondent has to demonstrate how the delay caused prejudice against him and he has to prove that petitioner has made false allegations. Thus, from the evidence on record petitioner is Mamatha G R vs Venkatesh Bellary K H on 17 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/1726353/ 17 able to prove that she left USA without informing the respondent that she intended to settle permanently in India due to the long standing abuse she and her children were subjected at the hands of the respondent. 45. Respondent has also argued that there is domestic relationship or shared household between himself and the petitioner hence this petition is not maintainable. He has relied on judgments reported in Smt.N.S.Leelavathi W/o Late S. Renuka Prasad & Ors. V/s Smt. Dr.R.Shilpa Brunda Also known as Ayesha Zubair W/o Dr. Zubair Khan 2019 0 Supreme(Kar) 1361 and Lakshmamma V/s Rajegowda 2023 0 Supreme (Kar) 987. Admittedly, parties are not divorced and they have lived together in a shared household at some point of time. It is argued by the learned counsel for the respondent that, some point of time means soon before filing of the petition it cannot be stretched beyond a limit. In this case parties have separated in June 2018 and this petition is filed in November 2018. Hence, this petition is filed soon after separation. Hence, they have a domestic relationship and the petition is maintainable. Hence, from the over all conspectus of the material before the Court petitioner is able to probabalize that the conduct of the respondent constitutes domestic violence as defined U/Sec.3 of PWDV Act. The respondent is duty bound to maintain the children.
texts.other_lawyer_arguments: The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kunapareddy @ Nookala Shank Balaji V/s Kunapareddy Swarna Kumari reported in (2016) 11 SCC 774 has held 53. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajanesh V/s Neha reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324 it is held that, when both spouses are earning sufficiently they have to contribute equally towards the expenses of the children.
